fields.text: A GLM architect lays out a small single-storey home from a brief - exactly seven named rooms (living room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, hallway, study, balcony), each placed in its own zone of a 3-by-3 grid (north-west to south-east) with one signature fixture drawn from above - a second GLM turns the layout into a plan-drawing brief, and Muse renders a flat architectural floor plan: black wall outlines on white, every room labelled in capitals inside its own space, every fixture drawn in its room. Then the loop closes: a Gemini vision checker reads the rooms back zone by zone with the fixtures it can see, a GLM auditor scores the layout against that read-back room by room - placed, wrong zone, missing, fixture drift, extras - and a Decide judge labels the plan planned to spec, zones drifted, rooms missing or wrong plan. The drawing has to answer to the layout, room by room. Four model families, four different jobs. See recipes/floor-plan-audit.md.

nodes.name: Floor plan, room-checked - plan, render, read back, audit

fields.text: One clean flat architectural floor plan for a small single-storey home with exactly seven rooms and no others: LIVING ROOM, KITCHEN, BEDROOM, BATHROOM, HALLWAY, STUDY and BALCONY. Read the plan as a 3-by-3 grid - north is the top, south the bottom, west the left, east the right - and every room sits in its own grid zone (north-west, north, north-east, west, centre, east, south-west, south or south-east), no two rooms sharing a zone. Hard constraints: every room labelled in clear capital letters inside its own space; every room shows exactly one signature fixture drawn from above; the front door opens into the HALLWAY; and no text anywhere except the home title and the seven room labels.

fields.system: You are a meticulous architect laying out a small single-storey home. The input is a brief for ONE floor plan with exactly seven rooms: LIVING ROOM, KITCHEN, BEDROOM, BATHROOM, HALLWAY, STUDY and BALCONY. Write ONE layout spec in this exact shape. First line: 'Home: <invented home name>'. Then exactly 7 numbered lines in this room order - 1 LIVING ROOM, 2 KITCHEN, 3 BEDROOM, 4 BATHROOM, 5 HALLWAY, 6 STUDY, 7 BALCONY - each in this shape: '<n>. <ROOM NAME> - <grid zone> - <one signature fixture>'. Grid zones come from a 3-by-3 grid (north-west, north, north-east, west, centre, east, south-west, south, south-east) and all seven zones must be different. Each room's signature fixture is one thing a floor plan can draw from above, chosen for that room: LIVING ROOM from L-shaped sofa, fireplace, bookshelf wall; KITCHEN from island counter, corner stove, farmhouse sink; BEDROOM from double bed, wardrobe wall, window seat; BATHROOM from bathtub, walk-in shower, double vanity; HALLWAY from long runner rug, coat cupboard, round hall table; STUDY from corner desk, reading armchair, tall bookcase; BALCONY from two deck chairs, planter row, small bistro set. The seven fixtures must all be different. Honour every hard constraint in the brief. Output the spec only, no preamble, no closing remarks.

nodes.name: Layout spec - GLM architect places the rooms

fields.system: You direct architectural plan drawing. The input is a home layout spec: a title line and 7 numbered rooms in a fixed order, each with a grid zone on a 3-by-3 grid and one signature fixture. Output ONE image prompt, under 130 words, for a clean flat architectural floor plan: a white background, black wall outlines seen directly from above, the home title printed across the top, exactly seven rooms and no others, each room placed in its spec grid zone (north-west is top-left, centre is the middle, south-east is bottom-right, and so on), each room labelled inside its own space in clear capital letters exactly as named in the spec, each room showing its one signature fixture drawn from above in simple plan symbols, a front door opening into the HALLWAY, no other rooms, text or numbers, no photographs, no people, no 3D perspective. Repeat every room name exactly as spelled in the spec. Output the prompt only.

nodes.name: Floor plan - Muse draws the home

fields.question: The text is a home layout spec: seven rooms in a fixed order, each placed in its own zone of a 3-by-3 grid (north-west to south-east) with one signature fixture. The image is a rendered floor plan that claims to show exactly that home. Which verdict fits? 'planned to spec' means every room is present, labelled, in its planned grid zone with its planned fixture. 'zones drifted' means all seven rooms are present but at least one sits in the wrong zone, or a fixture is clearly wrong. 'rooms missing' means at least one planned room cannot be found anywhere on the plan. 'wrong plan' means the image is not a seven-room floor plan of this spec at all. Judge the layout, not the styling.
fields.options:
planned to spec
zones drifted
rooms missing
wrong plan

fields.q: You are the plan checker in an architecture pipeline. Look at this floor plan and report ONLY what you can actually see. First give the plan title exactly as printed. Then, imagining the plan divided into a 3-by-3 grid (rows: north at the top, middle, south at the bottom; columns: west at the left, centre, east at the right), list the rooms in reading order - north-west, north, north-east, west, centre, east, south-west, south, south-east - one per line for each room you can see, each with its label exactly as printed, the grid zone its centre falls in, and the one signature fixture drawn inside it (for example a sofa, an island counter, a double bed, a bathtub, a runner rug, a desk, deck chairs). Then list any other rooms, labels or text visible anywhere in the image, if any. Do not guess at anything you cannot see - if you are unsure of a label, give your best reading and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any plan; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Plan check - Gemini reads the rooms

fields.system: You are a floor-plan auditor. The input gives a layout spec (a title line and 7 numbered rooms in a fixed order, each with a grid zone and one signature fixture), then the marker 'VISIBLE ON THE PLAN:' and a read-back of what a checker could actually see on the rendered plan. Compare the two, room by room. Output one line per spec room, in spec order (rooms 1 to 7), starting 'PLACED - ' if that room is visible in the same grid zone, 'WRONG ZONE - ' if it is visible but its centre falls in a different grid zone, or 'MISSING - ' if it cannot be found anywhere, followed by the room's name and its planned zone (for example 'zone centre'). After each room line, if the read-back gives its fixture differently from the spec, add one line starting 'DETAIL - ' naming the room and what differs. Then one 'EXTRA - ' line for each visible room that is not in the spec, if any. End with one line 'Summary: X of 7 placed.' Judge by room name and grid zone; a close spelling of the same label counts as the same room. Output the audit only, no preamble.
